evals.prompt: define an SLO for our checkout service
evals.expected_output: Picks an SLI measured close to the user (e.g. successful checkout completion, not just server-side 200s), sets the target below 100% derived from historical performance rather than a round number, states the resulting error budget in concrete units for the window, and writes a budget-exhaustion policy with a freeze threshold before it's needed.

evals.prompt: we keep arguing mid-incident about whether we're reliable enough to keep shipping
evals.expected_output: Diagnoses the missing piece as a pre-agreed, written budget-exhaustion policy (freeze threshold, mandatory reliability work, named escalation path) defined before an incident, not negotiated in the moment; also checks whether the SLO target was ever derived from data or just picked.

evals.prompt: let's set the SLO to five nines so everyone knows we take reliability seriously
evals.expected_output: Pushes back that a target above what the system has ever sustained means the budget starts already spent and the policy never has real teeth; recommends deriving the target from historical performance and user tolerance instead of picking an impressive-sounding number.
